t: AnyKey: A Key-Value SSD for All Workload Types
pb: Existing Key-Value SSD (KV-SSD) designs are optimized only for workloads where values are much larger than keys; when key sizes are relatively large (an unexplored but real workload class), the expanded key metadata causes significantly degraded performance and potentially unbounded metadata growth.
me: AnyKey redesigns the KV-SSD metadata management architecture to prevent metadata size from scaling with key size. It introduces a metadata-bounded key representation that separates key identity from the full key payload, storing only fixed-size key references (hashes or compact descriptors) in the primary metadata structures while managing full key payloads separately. This ensures metadata overhead remains bounded regardless of key size distribution.
nv: A metadata-bounded KV-SSD architecture that decouples key metadata size from actual key size, enabling uniform performance across both small-key and large-key workload types.
th: Workload-agnostic KV-SSD metadata management

t: OS2G: A High-Performance DPU Offloading Architecture for GPU-based Deep Learning with Object Storage
pb: Object storage for deep learning workloads imposes intensive CPU processing overhead and causes redundant data movements (DPU->host->GPU), consuming host resources and creating a data ingestion bottleneck that limits GPU utilization during training.
me: OS2G introduces a DPU offloading architecture that establishes a direct DPU-to-GPU data path, bypassing the host CPU entirely for object storage data delivery. It redesigns the object storage client to run on the DPU and exploits GPU-Direct or equivalent RDMA mechanisms to transfer data directly from the DPU's network interface into GPU memory. OS2G includes a DPU-side data processing pipeline (decompression, format conversion) to prepare DL-ready tensors before they enter GPU memory, eliminating the host CPU from the critical data path.
nv: End-to-end DPU-to-GPU direct data path for object storage in DL clusters that eliminates host CPU involvement and redundant data copies from the storage ingestion pipeline.
th: DPU-to-GPU direct data path for deep learning object storage

t: CXLfork: Fast Remote Fork over CXL Fabrics
pb: Remote process cloning across cluster nodes incurs high serialization and copying overhead, creating large cold-start latency for serverless functions and other scale-out workloads. Traditional fork() semantics do not map efficiently to distributed shared memory environments like CXL-attached memory.
me: CXLfork implements a remote fork interface that uses CXL-attached shared memory to achieve near-zero-serialization, zero-copy process cloning across nodes. It stores process state (pages, metadata) in globally-shared CXL memory for cluster-wide deduplication, so cloning a process on a remote node avoids transferring state over the network. Fine-grained tiering between local DRAM and CXL memory is supported, allowing hot pages to remain local while cold/shared pages reside in CXL memory. CXL-porter builds on top of CXLfork as an efficient horizontal autoscaler for serverless functions.
nv: Using CXL-attached globally-shared memory for cluster-wide process-state deduplication to achieve near-local-fork latency for remote process cloning.

mx.speedup: 2.26x over state-of-practice restore latency on average
mx.other: 87% reduction in local memory consumption on average

th: CXL-enabled zero-copy remote process cloning for serverless scale-out

t: Necro-reaper: Pruning away Dead Memory Traffic in Warehouse-Scale Computers
pb: A significant fraction of memory traffic in warehouse-scale computers (WSC) is unnecessary: it consists of writebacks of deallocated (dead) heap data and fetches of uninitialized data, neither of which carries useful information. Short-lived heap allocations larger than a cache line—common in WSC—exacerbate this problem.
me: Necro-reaper is a software/hardware co-design that introduces new ISA instructions to let the hardware skip unnecessary dead memory traffic without requiring hardware-level tracking of live/dead data. A profile-guided compiler analyzes allocation lifetimes and annotates call sites with the new instructions. A customized memory allocator extends these annotations to inform the hardware at deallocation time. The approach leverages WSC's existing vertical integration (shared hardware, OS, compiler, and allocator stack) to make the analysis and insertion of instructions practical.
nv: New ISA instructions that allow software (compiler + allocator) to signal dead heap regions to hardware, eliminating unnecessary writebacks and uninitialized-data fetches without hardware tracking.

mx.speedup: 6% geomean IPC increase across 10 WSC workloads
mx.other: 26% geomean memory traffic reduction

th: software-hardware co-design to eliminate dead memory traffic in warehouse-scale computers

t: Instruction-Aware Cooperative TLB and Cache Replacement Policies
pb: Modern server and data center applications have large instruction footprints that cause frequent instruction-side TLB and cache misses, with instruction TLB (iTLB) misses being particularly harmful because they cause pipeline stalls that block forward progress. Existing TLB and cache replacement policies treat instruction and data streams equivalently and do not account for the criticality of instruction accesses.
me: The paper proposes instruction-aware cooperative replacement policies that distinguish instruction accesses from data accesses in both the TLB and cache. The cooperative approach coordinates eviction decisions between the iTLB and the instruction cache (iCache), so that evicting a page from the iTLB also triggers or informs iCache eviction decisions and vice versa, reducing redundant refills. Replacement decisions are guided by instruction-access frequency and recency, with policy cooperation preventing the two structures from working at cross-purposes during instruction working set thrashing.
nv: Cooperative replacement policies that jointly manage iTLB and iCache evictions using instruction-access awareness, preventing the two structures from independently evicting and refilling the same instruction working set.

mx.other: reduced instruction TLB and cache miss rates in server workloads; specific numbers not in abstract

th: cooperative instruction-aware TLB and cache replacement for server workloads

t: OctoCache: Caching Voxels for Accelerating 3D Occupancy Mapping in Autonomous Systems
pb: OctoMap, a widely used octree-based 3D mapping framework for autonomous robots, suffers from slow update performance due to costly and irregular memory accesses into the octree structure. The lack of cache-friendly access patterns and parallelism limits real-time deployment on autonomous platforms such as UAVs.
me: OctoCache is a software-level acceleration system with three techniques: (1) optimized cache memory access patterns that restructure octree node traversal to improve spatial locality, (2) refined voxel ordering that reorders ray-casting updates to maximize cache reuse, and (3) workflow parallelization that concurrently executes independent map-update tasks. No custom hardware is introduced; the system targets general-purpose CPUs.
nv: Cache-aware voxel ordering combined with parallelized workflow scheduling to transform the inherently irregular OctoMap access pattern into a cache-friendly, concurrent workload without modifying the octree data structure.

mx.speedup: 45.63–88.01% on 3D construction; up to 3.02x in UAV navigation
mx.other: mission completion time reduced by up to 28%

th: cache-aware acceleration of octree-based 3D mapping

t: Earth+: On-Board Satellite Imagery Compression Leveraging Historical Earth Observations
pb: Satellite downlink capacity is so limited that over 90% of captured earth-observation images are never downloaded; existing on-board compression techniques treat each image independently and cannot exploit the rich temporal and spatial redundancy available across an entire satellite constellation.
me: Earth+ implements a change-detection-based compression pipeline on the satellite. Ground stations upload recently captured reference images from other satellites in the same constellation to each on-board satellite via the uplink. On-board processing compares each newly captured image against the latest matching reference image and transmits only the changed regions (delta encoding). The system manages reference image currency and on-board storage to ensure that references are temporally close to the captured images, maximizing delta sparsity and thus compression.
nv: First system to use cross-constellation reference images uploaded from ground stations to enable inter-satellite temporal redundancy exploitation for on-board compression, reducing downlink usage 3.3x over state-of-the-art without sacrificing image quality.

mx.speedup: 3.3x reduction in downlink usage vs. state-of-the-art on-board compression without quality loss or extra resource consumption

th: Cross-constellation reference-based on-board satellite imagery compression

t: ARC: Warp-level Adaptive Atomic Reduction in GPUs to Accelerate Differentiable Rendering
pb: During the backward pass of rasterization-based differentiable rendering (e.g., 3D Gaussian Splatting), gradient computation requires a large volume of atomic add operations to accumulate gradients from many Gaussian primitives into shared parameters, overwhelming the atomic units in the GPU L2 cache and causing long stalls that dominate training time.
me: ARC introduces warp-level adaptive atomic reduction, a GPU microarchitecture extension that intercepts atomic add operations at the warp level before they reach the L2 cache atomic units. Within a warp, threads targeting the same memory address are first reduced together using warp-level shuffle instructions (or a small dedicated reduction buffer), producing a single atomic operation per warp instead of one per thread. The approach adaptively decides whether to apply warp-level reduction based on detected contention levels, avoiding overhead when atomics are already sparse.
nv: Warp-level coalescing of atomic reduction operations before they reach the L2 cache, adaptively gated by contention detection, specifically targeting the gradient accumulation bottleneck in differentiable rendering.

mx.speedup: not stated in abstract

th: warp-level atomic reduction for differentiable rendering

t: StreamGrid: Streaming Point Cloud Analytics via Compulsory Splitting and Deterministic Termination
pb: Point cloud processing accelerators generate frequent off-chip memory traffic because conventional line-buffer streaming techniques—which eliminate off-chip traffic for image-based workloads—cannot be applied to point clouds due to their irregular, non-grid computation patterns that cause unpredictable data access boundaries and non-deterministic termination conditions.
me: StreamGrid introduces two techniques: compulsory splitting, which partitions the point cloud spatial domain into fixed-size grid cells that guarantee bounded on-chip working sets despite irregular neighborhoods; and deterministic termination, which statically determines when each streaming computation unit finishes processing its spatial partition, enabling on-chip buffering without deadlock or stall. StreamGrid combines these into a framework with an automated on-chip buffer size optimizer that minimizes SRAM under a given accuracy constraint.
nv: Compulsory spatial splitting paired with deterministic termination conditions that together enable fully-streaming point cloud processing with conventional line-buffer discipline despite irregular point cloud access patterns.

mx.speedup: 10.0x over state-of-the-art accelerators
mx.energy_or_tops_w: 3.9x energy efficiency over state-of-the-art accelerators; 40.5% energy reduction vs. baselines

th: streaming point cloud analytics via spatial splitting and deterministic termination

t: PIM Is All You Need: A CXL-Enabled GPU-Free System for Large Language Model Inference
pb: LLM inference is memory-bound (GEMV-dominated decoding stage with ~21% GPU compute utilization on Llama2-70B), yet modern GPU/TPU systems are optimized for compute throughput; simultaneously, large KV-cache requirements per user limit batch sizes, and CXL- or DRAM-density-reduced PIM architectures individually lack sufficient memory capacity or scalability for trillion-parameter LLMs.
me: CENT (CXL-ENabled GPU-Free sysTem) uses a hierarchical PIM-PNM architecture deployed across 32 CXL devices interconnected via a CXL 3.0 switch. Each CXL device contains 16 GDDR6-PIM memory chips (two PIM channels each) housing near-bank MAC reduction-tree processing units (16 MAC units/PU, BF16, 32 GFLOPS/PIM channel), plus PNM units including 32 accumulators, 32 reduction trees, 32 Taylor-series exponent accelerators, and 8 BOOM-2-wide RISC-V cores for non-MAC operations. MAC operations (>99% of arithmetic) execute near-bank; Softmax, RMSNorm, square root, and RoPE are handled by PNM. A custom CXL ISA (MAC_ABK, WR_GB, SEND_CXL, BCAST_CXL, etc.) orchestrates computation and data movement. LLM parallelism is implemented via pipeline parallel (PP: each transformer block to one CXL device, multiple prompts pipelined) and tensor parallel (TP: transformer block partitioned across all devices using broadcast/gather over CXL) mappings, with hybrid TP-PP for QoS balance. The CXL protocol is extended with a broadcast primitive via a reserved H-slot header code in port-based routing flits.
nv: A GPU-free hierarchical PIM-PNM architecture scaled via CXL 3.0 that exploits GDDR6-PIM internal bandwidth (512 TB/s aggregate) to achieve 2.3x higher LLM inference throughput than 4x A100 GPUs at 2.9x lower energy and 5.2x better TCO, with a novel CXL broadcast primitive enabling scalable collective communication across PIM devices.

mx.speedup: 2.3x end-to-end throughput over 4x A100 80GB GPUs (throughput-critical); 4.6x latency reduction (batch=1); 3.3x decoding throughput at 32K context
mx.area: CXL controller: 19.0 mm2 at 7nm; custom logic: 7.85 mm2 at 28nm
mx.other: 5.2x tokens per dollar (TCO); CENT owned TCO $0.73/hr vs GPU $1.76/hr; rental TCO $1.05/hr vs $5.45/hr

th: CXL-scaled PIM-PNM architecture for GPU-free LLM inference

t: PAPI: Exploiting Dynamic Parallelism in Large Language Model Decoding with a Processing-In-Memory-Enabled Computing System
pb: LLM decoding kernels dynamically shift between memory-bound and compute-bound behavior as request parameters (batch size, sequence length, sampling strategy) change at runtime, making static assignment of kernels to either PIM units or GPU-like compute accelerators suboptimal. Furthermore, existing PIM units are designed with a one-size-fits-all approach that fails to exploit the heterogeneity within memory-bound LLM kernels.
me: PAPI introduces a heterogeneous computing system combining PIM units embedded in DRAM with compute-centric accelerators (GPU-like), and a runtime that dynamically profiles kernel characteristics and remaps each kernel to the most suitable processing element at runtime. The PIM units are co-designed with awareness of intra-PIM heterogeneity to efficiently handle diverse memory-bound kernel patterns (e.g., matrix-vector products, attention, gating). A dynamic parallelism scheduler dispatches work to PIM or compute units based on real-time parameter changes driven by user or system demands.
nv: Runtime dynamic kernel-to-hardware mapping that responds to changing LLM decoding workload characteristics, combined with heterogeneity-aware PIM unit design to exploit intra-PIM variance in memory-bound kernels.

mx.other: Not stated in abstract

th: dynamic PIM-GPU scheduling for LLM decoding

t: Simplifying and Accelerating NOR Flash I/O Stack for RAM-Restricted Microcontrollers
pb: NOR flash file systems for RAM-restricted microcontrollers migrate block-level data organization and wear leveling logic from RAM into flash, introducing fine-grained block-level management that causes frequent index updates and full-device scans. This results in severe I/O amplification that worsens when the management layers are decoupled across the I/O stack.
me: The paper redesigns the NOR flash I/O stack to eliminate the decoupled block-level management abstraction, instead employing coarse-grained, integrated data organization that reduces index update frequency. Wear leveling is restructured to operate at a coarser granularity aligned with the NOR flash erase unit, avoiding the fine-grained scanning overhead. The resulting simplified stack collapses previously separate software layers to reduce coupling and I/O amplification jointly.
nv: Collapsing decoupled block-level management layers into a unified, coarse-grained I/O stack design that jointly eliminates index-update amplification and wear-leveling scan overhead for NOR flash on microcontrollers.

mx.other: I/O amplification reduction (details in full paper)

th: simplified NOR flash I/O stack for microcontrollers

t: Wave: Offloading Resource Management to SmartNIC Cores
pb: Userspace system software tasks (kernel thread scheduling, memory management, RPC stacks) consume scarce host CPU cores in cloud servers, reducing the compute available to paying tenants. Existing SmartNIC offload frameworks require custom APIs and cannot handle microsecond-scale system software latencies without host CPU involvement.
me: Wave is a framework that runs existing Linux userspace system software (unchanged or minimally modified) as processes/agents on mid-tier SmartNIC ARM cores. It introduces a new host-SmartNIC communication API designed to support microsecond-scale decision latencies, enabling offload of preemption-sensitive tasks such as the kernel thread scheduler. The framework uses Linux userspace system interfaces to align host OS functionality with SmartNIC capabilities, and avoids requiring custom kernel modifications on the host side.
nv: A general framework and microsecond-latency host-SmartNIC communication API that enables offloading of latency-sensitive userspace system software (scheduling, memory management, RPCs) to SmartNIC ARM cores with minimal code changes.

mx.speedup: 11.2% VM performance improvement from offload
mx.other: Saves 16 host cores (memory management), 8 host cores (RPC); 1.1%-7.4% perf overhead vs on-host

th: SmartNIC offload of userspace system software

t: Virtuoso: Enabling Fast and Accurate Virtual Memory Research via an Imitation-based Operating System Simulation Methodology
pb: Existing virtual memory (VM) simulation tools either lack accuracy in modeling OS software components (e.g., page table walks, TLB shootdowns, OS scheduling interactions) or are too slow and complex to prototype hardware/OS co-designs spanning the hardware/software boundary.
me: Virtuoso introduces an imitation-based OS simulation methodology where a lightweight simulator imitates the behavior of a full OS by training on traces of OS decisions (page allocation, eviction, TLB management) captured from real OS runs, then replaying those decisions with hardware-accurate timing in a fast simulation framework. This enables rapid iteration over hardware/OS co-design points without full OS simulation overhead.
nv: Using an imitation learning approach to reproduce OS virtual memory behavior accurately within a fast architectural simulator, avoiding the need for full OS simulation.

mx.other: not stated in abstract

th: imitation-based OS simulation for virtual memory research

t: ZRAID: Leveraging Zone Random Write Area (ZRWA) for Alleviating Partial Parity Tax in ZNS RAID
pb: ZNS SSD RAID systems must manage partial parity for incomplete stripes; prior approaches log partial parity in reserved zones, creating throughput bottlenecks and exacerbating write amplification that reduces SSD lifetime.
me: ZRAID exploits the Zone Random Write Area (ZRWA), a small random-write buffer region within ZNS SSDs, to buffer and consolidate partial parity in-place before committing full stripes to sequential zones. By using ZRWA as a transient parity staging area, ZRAID avoids persistent partial parity logging to reserved zones, eliminating the associated throughput bottleneck and write amplification. The system coordinates ZRWA usage across multiple ZNS drives to maintain RAID consistency.
nv: Using ZNS ZRWA buffers as transient in-device parity staging to eliminate partial parity logging overhead in ZNS RAID without reserved zones.

mx.other: not stated in abstract; claims throughput improvement and write amplification reduction

th: ZRWA-based partial parity elimination in ZNS RAID

t: Aqua: Network-Accelerated Memory Offloading for LLMs in Scale-Up GPU Domains
pb: LLM inference under bursty request patterns exhausts GPU memory, causing serving engines to use admission control that renders them unresponsive; preemptive time-sliced scheduling requires KV-cache paging that incurs high overhead and reduces throughput.
me: Aqua is a GPU memory management framework that uses the high-bandwidth scale-up network (NVLink/NVSwitch fabric within a server) as a fast memory offloading path for paging LLM inference state (KV caches). When a prompt is preempted, Aqua pages its KV cache over the scale-up network to remote GPU memory on other nodes rather than to slow host DRAM or NVMe, dramatically reducing paging latency. A scheduling layer enables preemptive time-sliced prompt execution on top of this low-overhead paging mechanism.
nv: Using the intra-server scale-up GPU interconnect (NVLink fabric) as a fast KV-cache paging path to enable low-overhead preemptive LLM scheduling without throughput loss.

mx.speedup: 4x throughput improvement over single long prompt baseline; 20x responsiveness improvement vs state-of-the-art
mx.other: evaluated on 8x NVIDIA H100 80GB GPU server

th: network-accelerated KV-cache paging for responsive LLM serving

t: ByteFS: System Support for (CXL-based) Memory-Semantic Solid-State Drives
pb: Memory-semantic SSDs expose both byte-addressable (via PCIe/CXL load/store) and block interfaces simultaneously, but existing software systems are designed for either NVM on the processor memory bus or block-interface SSDs, and cannot efficiently exploit the unique dual-interface characteristics and distinct performance profiles of memory-semantic SSDs.
me: ByteFS is a file system designed specifically for CXL-based memory-semantic SSDs. It exploits the byte interface for metadata and small random accesses (latency-sensitive operations) while using the block interface for large sequential data transfers (throughput-sensitive operations), routing operations to the appropriate interface based on access pattern and size. ByteFS introduces new OS abstractions (allocation, caching, I/O path) that account for the asymmetric performance characteristics of the two interfaces and the persistent byte-addressable semantics provided by the device.
nv: A file system that dual-routes operations between byte and block interfaces of memory-semantic SSDs based on access characteristics, with OS abstractions specifically designed for CXL-attached NAND flash memory semantics.

mx.other: not stated in abstract

th: OS file system support for CXL memory-semantic SSDs

t: Practical Federated Recommendation Model Learning Using ORAM with Controlled Privacy
pb: Federated learning (FL) for recommendation models is impractical because the large embedding tables require each user to access a tiny fraction of table entries, and hiding those access patterns via ORAM incurs prohibitive latency and SSD wear. Existing ORAM-based approaches have latency and SSD lifetime overheads that make them undeployable at scale.
me: FEDORA places the large ORAM structure on SSDs rather than DRAM, using SSD-friendly access optimizations to reduce write amplification and wear. It introduces epsilon-FDP (Federated Differential Privacy), a formal framework that trades off ORAM privacy strength against performance by allowing a controlled, quantified privacy budget, reducing the number of ORAM operations required. The system also supports modern FL operation modes (e.g., asynchronous and partial participation) so it integrates with production FL pipelines.
nv: Epsilon-FDP is a new formal privacy notion that explicitly balances ORAM obliviousness against performance cost, enabling practical SSD-backed ORAM for federated recommendation training.

mx.speedup: up to 24x latency reduction; 5x average latency improvement over baseline
mx.other: over 1000x SSD lifetime improvement (peak); 158x average SSD lifetime improvement

th: ORAM-backed federated learning for recommendation models

t: ASDR: Exploiting Adaptive Sampling and Data Reuse for CIM-based Instant Neural Rendering
pb: Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) inference exhibits irregular memory access patterns and high computational overhead, making it unsuitable for low-latency, power-efficient deployment on edge devices. Standard compute architectures cannot bridge the gap between NeRF's memory-bound irregular accesses and the immediacy/power requirements of practical neural rendering.
me: ASDR maps NeRF inference onto computing-in-memory (CIM) arrays to address the memory access bottleneck by performing computation near data storage, eliminating costly DRAM transfers. Adaptive sampling reduces the number of points sampled per ray dynamically based on scene complexity, cutting redundant computation. Data reuse strategies exploit spatial and temporal coherence across adjacent rays and frames to avoid redundant CIM macro activations. Together, these techniques reduce both the number of operations and the energy per operation on the CIM substrate.
nv: Co-designing adaptive ray sampling and cross-ray data reuse specifically for CIM array execution to simultaneously reduce irregular access overhead and compute volume in NeRF inference.

mx.speedup: not stated quantitatively in abstract

th: CIM-accelerated neural radiance field inference with adaptive sampling

t: Systematic CXL Memory Characterization and Performance Analysis at Scale
pb: CXL-attached memory introduces sub-microsecond latency overheads (140-410 ns) relative to local DRAM, but the performance impact across diverse devices, CPU platforms, and workloads is poorly understood, including tail latencies, prefetcher behavior, and bottleneck localization.
me: Melody is a characterization framework that runs 265 workloads across 4 real CXL devices, 5 CPU platforms, and 7 injected latency levels to comprehensively profile CXL memory performance. It introduces SPA (Sub-operation Performance Analysis), a novel methodology that decomposes memory access latency into sub-operations to pinpoint CXL-specific bottlenecks. Melody also measures and discloses CXL tail latency distributions for the first time, and characterizes CPU hardware prefetcher effectiveness (and failures) under CXL latency conditions.
nv: SPA is the first technique to pinpoint CXL memory bottlenecks at sub-operation granularity, and Melody provides the first systematic, multi-device, multi-CPU, multi-latency CXL characterization including tail latency disclosure.

mx.other: CXL latency range: 140-410 ns sub-microsecond; 265 workloads, 4 CXL devices, 5 CPU platforms, 7 latency levels evaluated

th: Systematic CXL memory performance characterization

t: Fusion: An Analytics Object Store Optimized for Query Pushdown
pb: Disaggregated cloud storage uses erasure coding that partitions analytics file objects into fixed-size blocks across storage nodes; when query predicates are pushed down to storage (computation pushdown), the storage system must reassemble objects across nodes, incurring high network latency that undermines pushdown's intended benefits for ad-hoc and highly-selective OLAP queries.
me: Fusion is an analytics object store that co-designs storage layout and query pushdown execution for erasure-coded environments. It reorganizes how analytics file objects (e.g., Parquet files) are partitioned and distributed across storage nodes so that query-relevant data stripes can be accessed and evaluated locally at storage nodes without full object reassembly. Pushdown execution is coordinated across storage nodes in a way that respects erasure coding boundaries, enabling predicate evaluation close to data while minimizing cross-node communication.
nv: Co-designing erasure-coded object storage layout with query pushdown execution so predicates can be evaluated at storage nodes without full object reassembly.

mx.speedup: not stated quantitatively in abstract
mx.other: reduced network latency for selective OLAP queries (not quantified in abstract)

th: Erasure-coding-aware analytics object store for query pushdown

t: Data Cache for Intermittent Computing Systems with Non-Volatile Main Memory
pb: Energy-harvesting embedded systems with non-volatile main memory (NVM) must checkpoint frequently to cover Write After Read (WAR) data hazards, incurring both high runtime overhead and excessive NVM writes; existing data cache solutions do not integrate WAR detection and require additional hardware or software memory trackers.
me: NACHO integrates WAR dependency detection directly into the data cache controller, eliminating the need for a separate memory tracker. When a cached dirty line is read after being written by NVM (a WAR hazard), the cache itself identifies and handles the dependency without a side-channel tracking structure. This co-design reduces checkpoint frequency (because fewer WARs escape detection) and reduces NVM writes (because dirty data is buffered in the volatile cache and written to NVM only at checkpoint time or on eviction), cutting both runtime and write wear.
nv: Embedding WAR dependency detection logic directly into the data cache, removing the external memory tracker required by prior intermittent computing systems.

mx.speedup: 54% average runtime overhead reduction vs. state-of-the-art cache-based intermittent computing
mx.other: 82% reduction in NVM writes vs. cache-less system; 18% average reduction vs. prior cache-based systems

th: WAR-integrated data cache for intermittent NVM-based embedded systems

t: Affinity-based Optimizations for TFHE on Processing-in-DRAM
pb: Fully Homomorphic Encryption over the Torus (TFHE) is a compute- and bandwidth-intensive workload; when mapped to Processing-in-Memory (PIM/HBM) architectures, existing accelerators over-exploit parallelism at the expense of data affinity, causing excessive remote data accesses (RDAs) that degrade performance due to PIM's limited inter-bank communication bandwidth.
me: The paper applies algorithmic optimizations to TFHE to restructure its sub-tasks (bootstrapping, key-switching, NTT/FFT operations) so that data accessed together is co-located on the same PIM vault or bank. An offline scheduler analyzes the affinity patterns of TFHE sub-tasks—determining which operands are used together and how frequently—and derives an optimal scheduling order that minimizes RDAs while maintaining sufficient parallelism. The approach is validated on a variant of an existing PIM-HBM device with minimal hardware modifications and evaluated on a real FPGA-based PIM system emulator.
nv: An affinity-pattern-driven offline scheduling framework for TFHE on PIM that minimizes remote data accesses by co-scheduling operations with shared data onto the same PIM units.

mx.speedup: 4.24x to 209x over prior TFHE accelerators on real-world benchmarks

th: Affinity-aware scheduling of TFHE on processing-in-DRAM to minimize remote accesses

t: Skia: Exposing Shadow Branches
pb: Modern processors using Fetch Directed Instruction Prefetching (FDIP) suffer from Branch Target Buffer (BTB) misses for instructions that have been previously decoded and evicted, causing the Branch Prediction Unit (BPU) to fail to recognize branches and either skip prefetching or speculate down wrong paths. These BTB misses stall the front-end and pollute the L1-I cache, a critical bottleneck for complex datacenter applications with large code footprints.
me: Skia introduces 'shadow branches': lightweight metadata structures that expose BTB-evicted branch information to the FDIP engine without restoring full BTB entries. When a branch is decoded and later evicted from the BTB, Skia retains shadow branch records (address and target hints) in a separate, higher-capacity structure. The FDIP engine consults these shadow records to continue speculative fetching along correct paths even when a BTB miss would otherwise halt prefetching or cause misdirection. This avoids both missed prefetches and wrong-path pollution of the L1-I cache.
nv: Exposing evicted BTB branch information as lightweight 'shadow branch' records that enable FDIP to continue correct speculative prefetching across BTB misses without full BTB entry restoration.
th: instruction prefetch via shadow branch exposure

t: Accelerating Retrieval-Augmented Generation
pb: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines for LLMs suffer from high latency in the retrieval phase due to expensive nearest-neighbor search over large knowledge bases, and existing profiling of the interplay between retrieval accuracy and generation phase cost is lacking. The choice between exact and approximate retrieval is not well characterized in terms of end-to-end latency vs. accuracy.
me: The paper profiles several RAG execution pipelines to characterize the complex interplay between retrieval and generation phases. It demonstrates that exact nearest-neighbor search, though more expensive in isolation, can outperform approximate retrieval end-to-end because an exact retrieval model selects a smaller, higher-precision set of documents, reducing the inference burden on the autoregressive generation stage. Based on this, the paper motivates and proposes hardware/system acceleration of exact nearest-neighbor search for RAG, using optimized data structures and computation strategies (specific details not available from abstract).
nv: Demonstrating that exact nearest-neighbor retrieval can reduce total RAG end-to-end inference latency compared to approximate retrieval by reducing the document set fed to the generative model, motivating hardware acceleration of exact search.

mx.other: end-to-end RAG latency reduction; specific numbers not in abstract

th: hardware acceleration of exact retrieval for RAG pipelines

t: HybridTier: an Adaptive and Lightweight CXL-Memory Tiering System
pb: CXL-based memory tiering systems must efficiently migrate pages between fast DRAM and slow CXL memory, but existing tiering systems fail to adapt to dynamically shifting hotness distributions and incur excessive memory and cache overhead from tracking metadata. Prior approaches use either long-term frequency or short-term recency but not both simultaneously.
me: HybridTier simultaneously tracks both long-term data access frequency and short-term access momentum to capture and adapt to shifting hotness distributions. To reduce memory overhead, it employs probabilistic access tracking with compact data structures that trade a small amount of tracking inaccuracy for significantly lower memory footprint. Cache overhead is minimized by organizing tracking metadata in data-locality-optimized lightweight structures that reduce cache misses during hotness lookups. Migration decisions combine both temporal signals for higher accuracy than either alone.
nv: Simultaneous dual-signal tracking (long-term frequency plus short-term momentum) combined with probabilistic metadata to achieve high hotness accuracy at minimal memory and cache overhead in CXL tiering.

mx.speedup: up to 91%, 19% geomean over prior tiering systems
mx.other: 2.0-7.8x less memory overhead, 1.7-3.5x fewer cache misses vs. prior systems

th: adaptive CXL memory tiering with dual-signal probabilistic tracking

t: M5: Mastering Page Migration and Memory Management for CXL-based Tiered Memory Systems
pb: CXL DRAM has 2-3x higher access latency than DDR DRAM, requiring effective page migration between tiers. Existing CPU-driven page-migration solutions misclassify warm pages as hot pages, fail to handle sparse hot-word pages (where only a small fraction of words in a page are hot), and incur high profiling overhead that can itself degrade application performance.
me: M5 implements a CXL-driven profiling solution that precisely and transparently counts accesses to every 4KB page and 64B cache-line word in CXL DRAM using hardware-based hot-page and hot-word trackers embedded in the CXL controller. Unlike CPU-driven approaches that rely on perf counters or OS page-fault sampling (which conflate warm and hot pages), the CXL controller observes all accesses on the CXL interconnect at cache-line granularity. The hot-page and hot-word trackers enable targeted migration: hot words can be promoted individually (sub-page granularity) for applications with sparse hot pages, avoiding unnecessary full-page migrations.

t: Hierarchical Prefetching: A Software-Hardware Instruction Prefetcher for Server Applications

t: PUSHtap: PIM-based In-Memory HTAP with Unified Data Storage Format
pb: Hybrid transaction/analytical processing (HTAP) systems cannot simultaneously achieve workload-specific optimization, performance isolation, and data freshness because OLTP demands row-store format while OLAP demands column-store format, and existing solutions (single format, multi-instance with rebuilding, or mixed delta-store) compromise at least one goal.

mx.other: Memory reduction from 14.34 Mbits to 288 Kbits; microsecond latency; nanosecond jitter

th: Memory-efficient Time-Aware Shaper via per-flow dynamic rule generation

t: NDFT: Accelerating Density Functional Theory Calculations via Hardware/Software Co-Design on Near-Data Computing System
pb: Linear-response time-dependent DFT (LR-TDDFT) is memory-bound with constant data movement between host and heterogeneous accelerators (GPU, FPGA, Sunway), creating substantial data movement overhead that dominates compute-optimized kernels.
me: NDFT proposes a near-data processing (NDP) framework that partitions LR-TDDFT tasks across CPU and NDP units optimally, offloading each computation phase to the most suitable processing element. Critical kernels undergo hardware/software co-optimization on the CPU-NDP system to further reduce data movement and latency.
nv: First near-data processing framework for LR-TDDFT that partitions workload across CPU and on-chip NDP units to minimize host-memory data movement, achieving 5.2x speedup over CPU and 2.5x over GPU.

mx.speedup: 5.2x vs CPU, 2.5x vs GPU

th: memory-bound HPC acceleration via near-data processing

t: Supporting Register-based Addressing Modes for in-DRAM PIM ISAs
pb: In-DRAM Processing-in-Memory architectures incur two critical overheads: PIM code offloading to memory and data transfers between CPU and memory, limiting speedup potential for DNN inference despite eliminating compute-memory bottleneck.
me: Two register-based addressing modes—indexed and base-offset—are added to DMA descriptor-based in-DRAM PIM ISAs. These modes reduce CPU-memory transfer overhead and PIM code offloading cost by enabling efficient descriptor composition and reducing descriptor complexity.
nv: First register-based addressing mode support for DMA-based in-DRAM PIM ISAs, significantly reducing control overhead and achieving 1.94x speedup with minimal area/power cost.

mx.speedup: 1.94x vs baseline PIM

th: register-based addressing for in-DRAM PIM acceleration

t: 333-eDRAM - 3T Embedded DRAM Leveraging Monolithic 3D Integration of 3 Transistor Types: IGZO, Carbon Nanotube and Silicon FETs
pb: Embedded DRAM design faces fundamental trade-offs between high density, high retention time, high endurance, low access latency, low access energy, and low static leakage power. Traditional single-material DRAM cannot simultaneously optimize all of these dimensions.
me: 333-eDRAM uses monolithic 3D integration of three FET types: IGZO FETs (ultra-low leakage for high retention), Carbon Nanotube FETs (high drive current for fast access), and Silicon CMOS (efficient peripherals). The design co-optimizes all key metrics including EADP (energy-area-delay product) with full physical layout at 7nm. Evaluation includes cycle-accurate simulation and SPICE models calibrated to experimental data.
nv: Monolithic 3D integration of heterogeneous materials (IGZO, CNT, Si) to simultaneously achieve high density, retention, endurance, speed, energy efficiency, and low leakage in a single eDRAM design.
th: Heterogeneous-material 3D integration for multi-objective eDRAM optimization

t: Late Breaking Results: Versatile 4:1 Multiplexer Using 1T1R RRAM Crossbar for High Speed In-Memory Computing
pb: In-memory computing with RRAM crossbars requires efficient logic operations, but existing 4:1 multiplexer designs require 10 steps, limiting the speed of computations performed directly in memory.
me: The paper proposes a NAND-based 4:1 multiplexer design in a 1T1R RRAM crossbar that completes execution in 3 steps instead of 10. The approach extends to full adders, full subtractors, and 1-bit comparators, reducing clock cycles by 75% compared to state-of-the-art designs. Although memristor count increases, the computational delay reduction makes this promising for in-memory computing.
nv: NAND-logic-based 4:1 multiplexer reducing execution steps from 10 to 3 in RRAM crossbars, enabling fast in-memory logic operations.
th: Fast in-memory logic using optimized RRAM crossbar multiplexers

t: GraphAccel: An In-Storage Accelerator for Efficient Graph-Based Vector Similarity Search Using Page Packing and Speculative Search Optimization
pb: Graph-based approximate vector similarity search (essential for retrieval-augmented generation and AI applications) often stores large-scale graphs on SSDs, but SSD page access patterns and latency underutilize available bandwidth and compute resources.
me: GraphAccel is an in-storage accelerator integrated into SSDs that optimizes graph search through two key mechanisms: (1) page packing that reduces SSD page accesses per query by co-locating related graph nodes, and (2) speculative search that maximizes utilization of idle SSD chips and channels by prefetching and processing multiple paths in parallel. The approach is compared against DiskANN and DiskANN++.
nv: In-storage graph acceleration using page packing and speculative prefetching to maximize throughput utilization in SSD-based vector search systems.
th: In-storage acceleration for SSD-based graph vector search

t: BiNeuroRAM: Energy-Efficient ReRAM-Based PIM for Accurate Bipolar Spiking Neural Network Acceleration
pb: Existing ReRAM-based neuromorphic accelerators suffer from high sensing power and accuracy degradation when running spiking neural networks, limiting their deployment.
me: BiNeuroRAM uses ReRAM-based processing-in-memory with three innovations: (1) support for spike-tracing bipolar-integrate-and-fire (ST-BIF) neurons enabling higher accuracy; (2) low-power voltage sense amplifier (LPVSA) reducing ReRAM read power by 14.7-58.2x via optimized sensing; (3) asynchronous micro-architecture exploiting event-driven SNN sparsity to maximize throughput.
nv: First ReRAM accelerator supporting ST-BIF neurons while reducing sensing power by orders of magnitude through specialized LPVSA design.
th: ReRAM-based neuromorphic computing with advanced neuron models

t: StreamCSD: SSD-Autonomous Stream Management via In-Storage Content Learning
pb: Write amplification from garbage collection during SSD operation degrades performance and shortens lifespan; existing stream management solutions require host-side changes, hindering adoption.
me: StreamCSD uses compression ratios from embedded compressors in computational storage drives (CSDs) as a proxy for data compressibility. Applies streaming K-means to cluster data into streams based on compression similarity, enabling autonomous stream assignment without host involvement.
nv: First SSD-autonomous stream management leveraging in-storage compression data to infer semantic properties for stream assignment.

mx.other: write amplification reduction from 1.7 to 1.06

th: Autonomous SSD stream management via compression-based clustering

t: MemSens: Significantly Reducing Memory Overhead in Adjoint Sensitivity Analysis Using Novel Error-Bounded Lossy Compression
pb: Adjoint sensitivity analysis requires storing all state vectors and Jacobian matrices at every time step for gradient computation, leading to prohibitive memory costs for large-scale dynamic systems and long simulations.
me: Proposes error-bounded lossy compression of state information that exploits spatiotemporal characteristics of circuit simulation data. Combines specialized compression algorithms with stringent error control mechanisms to reduce stored state volume while maintaining adjoint solution accuracy.
nv: First adjoint sensitivity analysis method using lossy compression with error bounds to preserve numerical correctness.

mx.other: 100x memory overhead reduction, accuracy preservation

th: Error-bounded compression for adjoint simulation

t: PUFiM: A Robust and Efficient FeFET-Based Security Solution Merging Physical Unclonable Function with Compute-in-Memory for Edge AI
pb: CiM architectures for edge AI leak model weights stored in plaintext; while PUFs could provide key generation, existing approaches lack comprehensive key generation/delivery frameworks and incur high storage overhead for ciphertext.
me: PUFiM integrates ferroelectric FET (FeFET) PUFs with CiM arrays in unified architecture using multi-level cell (MLC) FeFETs for hybrid PUF+weight storage. Combines three innovations: (1) strong PUF co-designed with CiM for key generation and authentication; (2) high-density hybrid storage via MLC FeFETs avoiding separate ciphertext storage; (3) PUF enhancement techniques and novel mapping scheme for improved robustness.
nv: First work synergizing physical unclonable functions with CiM in unified array for end-to-end security without ciphertext storage overhead.

mx.other: compute density 9.7x, energy efficiency 1.2x, attack resilience to 10M samples

th: FeFET-based unified PUF and compute-in-memory for edge AI security

t: FineRR-ZNS: Enabling Fine-Granularity Read Refreshing for ZNS SSDs
pb: Zoned namespace SSDs lack read refreshing mechanisms to guarantee data reliability, and zone-level read refreshing incurs severe overhead due to large valid data movements, degrading I/O performance.
me: Proposes host-controlled fine-granularity read refreshing via metadata remapping at block level, includes zone reconstruction method to retrieve remapped data forming complete data, keeps remapped data available and prioritized for read access until next refresh cycle.
nv: Block-level metadata remapping approach enabling fine-granularity read refreshing in ZNS SSDs with efficient zone reconstruction, eliminating zone-level refresh overhead.

mx.other: Significantly enhanced read refreshing efficiency and I/O throughput vs. state-of-the-art ZenFS

th: Fine-granularity read refreshing for ZNS SSDs via block-level metadata remapping

t: 3D-SubG: A 3D Stacked Hybrid Processing Near/In-Memory Accelerator for Subgraph GNNs
pb: Subgraph Graph Neural Networks have complex irregular structures with numerous independent subgraphs, creating severe bandwidth bottlenecks and poor data reuse in conventional architectures, limiting throughput.
me: 3D stacks logic die with DRAM die via hybrid bonding; logic die employs SRAM-based processing-in-memory macros for computation density; bit-level non-zero gathering exploits graph sparsity; workload-balanced mapping allocates subgraphs to logic-DRAM blocks; distributed global pooling reduces inter-block data movements.
nv: 3D hybrid bonding integration of logic with DRAM using SRAM-based PIM macros, combined with sparsity-aware bit-level gathering and distributed pooling for subgraph GNNs.

mx.speedup: 146.11× performance vs. RTX 3090Ti

th: 3D hybrid bonding PIM accelerator for subgraph GNNs with sparsity and workload balancing

t: Efficient Edge Vision Transformer Accelerator with Decoupled Chunk Attention and Hybrid Computing-In-Memory
pb: Vision Transformers suffer from quadratic self-attention complexity, making them slow and resource-intensive for dense pixel-level predictions on edge devices; pyramid ViT architecture creates unbalanced workloads and poor hardware utilization.
me: Proposes decoupled chunk attention (DCA) in pipelined form to reduce off-chip memory access; combines SRAM-based computing-in-memory with RRAM nonvolatile storage; bit/element two-way-reconfigurable CIM macros adapt to varied pyramid ViT block sizes; fusion scheduling balances workload and minimizes intermediate memory.
nv: Decoupled chunk attention mechanism with pipelined execution and hybrid CIM-RRAM architecture featuring reconfigurable bit/element-level computation macros.

mx.speedup: 18.5×-217.1× on dense predictions
mx.other: 1.7×-7.4× memory access reduction; <1% performance degradation

th: Hybrid CIM-RRAM ViT accelerator with decoupled chunk attention and reconfigurable macros

t: Sphinx: A High-Performance Hybrid Index for Disaggregated Memory With Succinct Filter Cache
pb: Range indexes for disaggregated memory architectures suffer from excessive network round trips during tree traversal and inefficient node-based caching, limiting lookup performance for variable-length keys.
me: Sphinx replaces sequential tree traversal with parallel hash reads using an Inner Node Hash Table, reducing network round trips. A Succinct Filter Cache further minimizes network overhead while maintaining a small, coherent computing-side cache.
nv: Inner Node Hash Table transforms tree traversal into parallel hash operations, eliminating sequential network bottlenecks.
th: network-efficient indexing for disaggregated memory

t: Late Breaking Results: Less Sense Makes More Sense: In-Sensor Compressive Learning for Efficient Machine Vision
pb: High-resolution image sensors generate excessive data requiring quantization and transmission overhead, consuming energy inefficiently for downstream deep learning tasks.
me: A lightweight in-sensor compressive learning framework encodes raw images into low-dimensional representations using a 1-bit encoder co-optimized with downstream vision tasks. The encoder is integrated directly within the image sensor for task-specific feature extraction.
nv: 1-bit in-sensor encoder jointly optimized with downstream tasks achieves 10× data compression while maintaining task accuracy.
th: in-sensor compressive learning for efficient vision

t: All-in-Memory Stochastic Computing using ReRAM
pb: Stochastic computing bit-stream generators consume over 80% of system power and area; current solutions focus on gate optimization but ignore high data movement costs between memory and processor for bit-stream exchange.
me: All-in-memory stochastic computing leverages ReRAM physics to: (1) generate low-cost true random numbers and stochastic bit-streams in-place, (2) perform SC operations directly on ReRAM cells, and (3) convert bit-streams back to binary. ReRAM's robustness to errors complements SC's fault tolerance.
nv: In-place stochastic computing flow entirely within ReRAM eliminates bit-stream data movement and leverages ReRAM variability as source of randomness.
th: in-place stochastic computing using ReRAM physics

t: Guarder: A Stable and Lightweight Reconfigurable RRAM-based PIM Accelerator for DNN IP Protection
pb: RRAM-based processing-in-memory accelerators suffer from imprecise weights due to programming stochasticity, limiting model accuracy, and cannot effectively utilize conventional weight encryption/decryption IP protection schemes.
me: Guarder proposes a software-hardware co-design: (1) Hardware: 3T2R cells for reliable MAC operations and reconfigurable inverter operating voltages to encode encryption keys directly in RRAM, (2) Software: Contrastive training ensures high accuracy on authorized chips and degraded performance on unauthorized ones.
nv: Co-designed 3T2R RRAM PIM with encrypted-key inverter voltage encoding and contrastive training for DNN IP protection.
th: encrypted-RRAM PIM accelerator for DNN IP protection

t: An Efficient Compute-in-Memory based Accelerator for Point-based Point Cloud Neural Networks
pb: Point-based point cloud neural networks are computationally intensive and exhibit poor performance on resource-constrained edge devices due to irregular data access patterns and high memory bandwidth requirements.
me: Point-CIM proposes a reconfigurable CIM unit exploiting zero-bit-skipping sparsity, Voxel-Morton-sorted Partitioning (VMP) with Channel-wise Minimum base point selection for improved decomposition sparsity, and Bit-level Truncation Quantization (BTQ) for bit-width compression without extra hardware. Pre-decomposition data movement strategy reduces transfers between buffer and CIM array.
nv: Reconfigurable CIM architecture with bit-sparsity exploitation via feature decomposition and quantization-aware optimization for point cloud networks.
th: sparsity-exploiting CIM accelerator for point cloud networks

t: SeIM: In-Memory Acceleration for Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
pb: ANNS workloads bottleneck on memory bandwidth (extensive random access) and sorting (cross-memory-unit data dependencies), limiting throughput in CPU/GPU/ASIC-based systems and making them inefficient for RAG-based LLM inference.
me: Hierarchical in-memory architecture that offloads memory-bound parallel ANNS operations (vector loading, distance computation) to the memory bank level with minimal DRAM modifications, and places compute-bound sorting at the memory controller level with adaptive transmission filtering to reduce cross-unit data transfers during merge operations.
nv: Decomposition of ANNS operations across memory hierarchy levels (bank/controller) with unified execution model to reuse hardware and avoid redundant data movement.
th: hierarchical in-memory acceleration for ANNS via bank/controller-level partitioning

t: CXL-ECC: an Efficient LRC-based on-CXL-Memory-eXpander-Controller ECC to Enhance Reliability and Performance of DRAM Error Correction
pb: CXL Memory Expanders provide high-capacity, high-bandwidth memory but DRAM reliability remains underexplored; traditional RAID/replica-based fault tolerance incurs prohibitive CXL-fabric bandwidth overhead, degrading system performance.
me: Proposes on-CXL-Memory-Expander-Controller (CXL-MXC) ECC using Locally Recoverable Codes (LRC) as inter-channel ECC (IC-ECC), offloading ECC computation to the CXL expander itself to eliminate redundant CXL fabric traffic. Balances reliability with minimal bandwidth overhead.
nv: Offloading LRC-based ECC to the CXL expander controller to avoid redundant memory access requests in the fabric, achieving reliability without bandwidth amplification.

mx.other: Reliability 10^9× improved, bandwidth overhead 63.5%→3.4%, 12% perf gain

th: on-expander LRC-based ECC for CXL Memory bandwidth efficiency

t: McPAL: Scaling Unstructured Sparse Inference with Multi-Chiplet HBM-PIM Architecture for LLMs
pb: Monolithic PIM architectures cannot scale to very large LLMs (70B+) due to single-die memory footprint limits; LLM inference is memory-bound, and PIM can provide high memory bandwidth but scaling via larger dies hits power/yield constraints.
me: Multi-chiplet HBM-PIM architecture (McPAL) that decomposes arbitrary unstructured sparse weight matrices into multiple irregular sparse vectors, then routes non-skipped computations via in-memory butterfly network to standard PIM arrays. Vertically scales via 3D-HBM hierarchy (minimizing long-distance data travel) and horizontally via 2.5D IO chiplet (reducing die-to-die traffic and balancing sparse workload).
nv: Hierarchical multi-chiplet PIM scaling with in-memory butterfly network for arbitrary unstructured sparsity, avoiding monolithic bottlenecks.
th: hierarchical multi-chiplet PIM with butterfly network for scalable sparse LLM inference

t: CIM-BLAS: Computing-in-Memory Accelerator for BLAS
pb: Basic Linear Algebra Subprograms (BLAS) are foundational for scientific/engineering computing but are data-intensive, bottlenecked by limited memory bandwidth in CPUs and GPUs. Memory bandwidth is the primary constraint for level-1/2 BLAS operations and a significant bottleneck for level-3 operations.
me: First CIM accelerator for BLAS based on non-volatile memory (NVM). Features unified floating-point pipeline supporting high-precision arithmetic (to handle BLAS variety). Configurable dataflows support diverse BLAS functions (levels 1, 2, 3). Memory-bound operations execute directly in memory; compute-bound ops leverage PIM's high parallelism.
nv: First CIM-based BLAS accelerator with unified floating-point pipeline and configurable dataflows to support BLAS hierarchy.

mx.energy_or_tops_w: 2.6–24.1× energy efficiency vs. GPU for level-3 BLAS; orders of magnitude for level-1/2

th: CIM-based BLAS acceleration via high-precision unified floating-point pipeline

t: Efficient Weight Mapping and Resource Scheduling on Crossbar-based Multi-core CIM Systems
pb: Multi-core crossbar-based CIM systems (eFlash-based SoCs) must optimize for both latency and resource utilization. Key compiler challenges include high parallel processing overhead, suboptimal resource utilization, and inefficient crossbar array assignment for CNNs, resulting in poor latency and low array utilization.
me: Proposes resource scheduling strategy based on stream data processing to reduce intra-core and inter-core communication latency. Develops weight mapping strategy to maximize crossbar array utilization for CNN deployment. Applies stream-based processing to schedule data flows and reduce handoffs between cores.
nv: Stream-based resource scheduling combined with weight mapping strategy for crossbar utilization maximization in multi-core CIM systems.

mx.speedup: 76% latency reduction
mx.other: 30% resource utilization improvement, 94.7% array utilization

th: stream-based scheduling and weight mapping for multi-core CIM CNN acceleration

t: UPVSS: Jointly Managing Vector Similarity Search with Near-Memory Processing Systems
pb: Vector similarity search is bandwidth-bound in CPU-based systems; DRAM bandwidth becomes the critical bottleneck as data scales, limiting throughput in recommendation systems and LLM deployments.
me: Offloads similarity search to UPMEM near-memory processing units, distributing computation close to data to reduce core-to-memory data movement and maximize UPMEM's parallelism through architecture-aware workload distribution.
nv: Architecture-aware integration of vector search with UPMEM's distributed PIM capabilities to overcome bandwidth bottlenecks.

mx.speedup: system-level acceleration

th: PIM-accelerated vector similarity search

t: MIRACLE: Multimodal Information Retrieval via a Combined In-Memory Processing and Content Addressable Memory Approach
pb: Multimodal retrieval via neural feature extraction + similarity search is inefficient; cosine similarity on von Neumann wastes memory bandwidth, and pure hashing sacrifices accuracy due to modal heterogeneity.
me: Hybrid architecture combining in-memory random hashing (PIM) for fast approximate ranking and content-addressable memory (CAM) for parallel search space reduction, followed by final cosine reranking for accuracy recovery.
nv: PIM+CAM hybrid that leverages device-intrinsic hashing properties in memory while using CAM for efficient search reduction.
th: PIM+CAM hybrid for multimodal vector retrieval

t: MiniWear: Minimizing Flash Wear via Hybrid Persistent Cache for Extended EF-SMR Lifetime
pb: EF-SMR (Embedded-Flash SMR) systems combine NAND flash and Shingled Magnetic Recording disks to balance cost/performance, but flash endurance faces critical degradation due to high traffic-to-capacity ratios causing excessive wear.
me: MiniWear introduces a hybrid persistent cache (PC) composed of Flash-PC and SMR-PC tiers with fine-grained scheduling strategies. At hardware level, the PC is organized as dual tiers; at software level, customized scheduling manages PC resources efficiently. Proactive balancing strategy addresses resource idleness to maximize wear distribution across storage layers.
nv: First hybrid persistent cache architecture for EF-SMR systems with tiered flash/SMR organization and proactive resource balancing to extend flash lifetime.

mx.other: 66.67% flash wear reduction

th: hybrid persistent cache for flash wear reduction in EF-SMR

t: CXL-INTERPLAY: Unraveling and Characterizing CXL Interference in Modern Computer Systems
pb: Compute Express Link (CXL) enables memory/storage expansion but faces performance degradation when coexisting with conventional memory and storage systems; interference effects are largely unexplored in real hardware, creating blind spots in deployment.
me: CXL-Interplay systematically characterizes and analyzes interference from memory and storage systems on CXL using real CXL hardware. Employs performance counter analysis and kernel-level tracing for reverse-reasoning investigation of interference mechanisms. Proposes and evaluates mitigation solutions to reduce identified interference.
nv: First systematic characterization of CXL interference on real CXL hardware; first reverse-reasoning analysis using performance counters to understand interference mechanisms.

mx.other: Interference characterization, mitigation effectiveness

th: CXL interference characterization and mitigation

t: Late Breaking Results: On-the-Fly Hadamard Hypervector Processing for Efficient Hyperdimensional Computing
pb: Hyperdimensional Computing (HDC) requires expensive pre-generation or iterative O(N) search to find orthogonal hypervectors, creating bottleneck for hardware deployment; fixed precomputed vectors limit adaptability.
me: Introduces on-the-fly hypervector generation in hardware using Hadamard binary coefficients with O(1) complexity versus O(N) conventional search. Leverages unary computing and in-memory computing (IMC) to simplify encoding into addition-only operations after generation. ASIC implementation leverages Hadamard properties for efficient hardware realization.
nv: First O(1) on-the-fly Hadamard hypervector generation in hardware, replacing O(N) iterative search with direct generation via binary coefficients.

mx.other: Accuracy improvement, computational efficiency gains

th: O(1) Hadamard-based hypervector generation for HDC acceleration

t: PICK: An SRAM-based Processing-in-Memory Accelerator for K-Nearest-Neighbor Search in Point Clouds
pb: K-nearest neighbor (kNN) search on point clouds is computationally intense and memory-heavy, but off-chip memory access dominates latency and energy. Current approaches struggle with resource-constrained scenarios typical in edge AI and autonomous driving.
me: PICK is a PIM (processing-in-memory) architecture using bit-serial PIM (BS-PIM) to perform kNN search with on-chip SRAM, eliminating off-chip access. Includes: (1) bit-width clipping for bit-serial distance calculation with reduced latency; (2) filtering-and-selection strategy achieving approximately constant time for arbitrary k; (3) two-stage pipeline parallelizing distance calculation and top-k selection.
nv: Bit-serial PIM architecture with filtering-and-selection strategy and two-stage pipelining to achieve constant-time kNN selection within on-chip SRAM, eliminating off-chip memory bottleneck.
th: Bit-serial PIM architecture for accelerated kNN search in point clouds

t: ARCANE: Adaptive RISC-V Cache Architecture for Near-memory Extensions
pb: Von Neumann architectures suffer from data movement bottlenecks (extensive memory traffic, low throughput, poor energy efficiency). Existing accelerators improve performance but lack flexibility and require explicit data transfers; compute in-/near-memory solutions face usability challenges due to data placement constraints.
me: ARCANE integrates a tightly-coupled compute-near-memory coprocessor into the cache hierarchy via a RISC-V cache controller. The controller executes custom instructions from the host CPU using vector operations dispatched to near-memory vector processing units embedded within cache memory. Software-transparent synchronization and data mapping are automatically handled by the architecture.
nv: Cache-integrated near-memory computing via RISC-V ISA extensions with automatic data placement, eliminating explicit data management overhead.

mx.speedup: 30-84x for 8-bit data vs. baseline

th: cache-integrated near-memory computing with ISA abstraction

t: CIMFlow: An Integrated Framework for Systematic Design and Evaluation of Digital CIM Architectures
pb: Digital compute-in-memory (CIM) architectures promise DNN acceleration by addressing the memory wall, but lack comprehensive design and evaluation frameworks that cover both software (compilation) and hardware design spaces, and fail to address capacity constraints inherent in CIM systems.
me: CIMFlow is an integrated framework providing end-to-end workflow for implementing and evaluating DNN workloads on digital CIM. It bridges compilation and simulation infrastructures with flexible instruction set architecture (ISA) design. The framework addresses CIM capacity constraints through advanced partitioning and parallelism strategies in the compilation flow.
nv: Unified framework bridging compilation and simulation with advanced partitioning strategies specifically addressing digital CIM capacity constraints.

mx.other: enables systematic design space exploration of digital CIM architectures

th: integrated framework for digital CIM design and optimization

t: Device-Algorithm Co-Design of Ferroelectric Compute-in-Memory In-Situ Annealer for Combinatorial Optimization Problems
pb: Combinatorial optimization problems require O(n²) vector-matrix-vector multiplications for Ising energy computation and complex exponential annealing factors, making traditional annealers hardware-expensive and slow for large instances like Max-Cut with thousands of nodes.
me: A device-algorithm co-design using double-gate ferroelectric FET (DG FeFET) CiM crossbars with a novel incremental-E transformation that reduces VMV complexity from O(n²) to O(n) by computing energy changes incrementally; approximates exponential annealing with simplified fractional forms to enable efficient in-situ computation within a tunable back-gate annealing flow.
nv: Incremental-E transformation reducing Ising energy computation from O(n²) to O(n) combined with ferroelectric CiM substrate for native in-situ annealing.
th: ferroelectric CiM accelerator for efficient combinatorial optimization via complexity reduction

t: Me-MPK: Accelerating Krylov Subspace Solvers via Memory-efficient Matrix-Power Kernel
pb: Matrix-Power Kernels (MPK) for Krylov subspace methods rely on repeated SpMVs with the same matrix but suffer from data dependencies that block cache reuse and symmetric SpMVs incur data conflicts during shared-memory parallelization, limiting speedup on multi-core CPUs.
me: Me-MPK constructs a unified dependency graph for sparse matrices capturing all potential dependencies and conflicts; performs architecture-aware recursive partitioning into independent subgraphs with a separating subgraph that decouples conflicts; schedules subgraphs for parallel SpMV/symmetric-SpMV execution in order to maximize cache reuse while eliminating synchronization overhead.
nv: Unified dependency graph approach enabling simultaneous exploitation of matrix reuse and symmetry, paired with recursive partitioning to create conflict-free independent subgraphs for ordered parallel execution.
th: memory-efficient sparse solver via unified dependency-driven partitioning

t: In-Memory Arithmetic: Enabling Division with Stochastic Logic
pb: Efficient hardware division has been a long-standing challenge; traditional binary approaches require multiple cycles and complex control logic. Emerging in-memory computing faces additional obstacles: noise sensitivity, process variation, and the inherent difficulty of binary operations in noisy substrates.
me: The approach uses stochastic computing (SC) to implement division within an MTJ-based in-memory architecture; SC represents numbers as bitstreams and performs arithmetic through simple logic operations, naturally tolerating noise. MTJ memory provides the substrate for logic-in-memory operations, reducing the data movement penalty.
nv: Application of stochastic computing to in-memory division leveraging MTJ crossbars, achieving fault tolerance against process variation and noise inherent in emerging memory substrates.

mx.other: robustness demonstrated across process variation conditions

th: stochastic in-memory division for fault-tolerant analog/near-analog computing

t: WISEDRAM: A Reliable Bitwise In-DRAM Accelerator
pb: Processing-in-Memory (PIM) techniques in DRAM suffer from vulnerability to process variation and noise, internal cell leakage, and high latency in cell access, limiting real-world deployment of in-DRAM compute.
me: WISEDRAM uses one row of special X-cells to enable in-DRAM bulk-bitwise operations while retaining conventional DRAM cell access procedures for reliable reads/writes. This ensures reliability equivalent to standard DRAM while enabling parallel in-DRAM computation.
nv: First PIM approach that preserves conventional DRAM cell access procedures while enabling in-DRAM bitwise operations, ensuring reliability at standard DRAM levels.

mx.speedup: 71% faster XOR operations

th: Reliable in-DRAM bitwise accelerator leveraging X-cells

t: HIVE: A High-Priority Victim Cache for Accelerating GPU Memory Accesses
pb: GPU memory hierarchies suffer from high latency when victim caches are accessed as secondary L1D miss handlers, particularly for memory-intensive workloads.
me: HIVE redesigns the victim cache to handle memory requests before L1D access. High-priority victim cache provides direct low-latency memory request handling, bypassing the L1D cache for certain access patterns. Architectural modification prioritizes victim cache lookups for the most latency-critical requests.
nv: Victim cache hierarchy inversion: handling requests at victim cache level before L1D to reduce critical path latency.
th: Victim cache prioritization for GPU memory latency

t: Enabling Data-Deduplication-Assisted Data Relocation for Interlaced Magnetic Recording
pb: Interlaced Magnetic Recording (IMR) hard drives suffer degraded performance when updating data on overlapped tracks, requiring rewriting up to two tracks per update.
me: Leverages data deduplication metadata (reference counts) to guide data relocation in IMR drives. Deduplicated data (static unless references drop to one) can be placed/migrated to overlapped tracks without inducing future rewrites. Replaces frequency-based hot/cold tracking with deduplication-informed placement.
nv: First application of deduplication reference counts to data relocation in IMR drives, enabling zero-cost overlap placement.
th: Deduplication-aware data placement in IMR drives

t: VEDA: Efficient LLM Generation Through Voting-based KV Cache Eviction and Dataflow-flexible Accelerator
pb: LLM inference on edge devices faces memory and computational bottlenecks due to intensive KV cache requirements and variable sequence lengths, limiting deployment feasibility.
me: Algorithm-hardware-dataflow tri-optimization: (1) voting-based KV cache eviction identifies unimportant kv vectors adaptively, reducing cache size while maintaining accuracy; (2) flexible-product dataflow with runtime-reconfigurable PE array handles diverse matrix-vector dimensions; (3) element-serial scheduling for nonlinear ops (softmax, layernorm). Hardware complexity reduced from O(N) to O(1). Custom VEDA accelerator implementation.
nv: Adaptive KV cache voting for LLM inference combined with dataflow-flexible hardware for variable-dimension operations.
th: Adaptive KV cache and flexible dataflow for edge LLM inference

t: Can Short Hypervectors Drive Feature-Rich GNNs? Strengthening the Graph Representation of Hyperdimensional Computing for Memory-efficient GNNs
pb: Hyperdimensional computing (HDC) requires ultra-long hypervectors (tens of thousands of bits) to express rich features, creating a memory bottleneck that offsets HDC's computational efficiency.
me: CiliaGraph rebuilds HDC operations to overcome three GNN incompatibilities: (1) feature distortion via better encoding, (2) structural bias via weighted aggregation, (3) central-node vacancy via expanded supervision. Uses short hypervectors (hundreds of bits) with error-tolerant neural principles to maintain accuracy.
nv: First HDC-based GNN framework that breaks the long-vector consensus by proving hundreds of bits suffice for feature-rich graph learning.
th: Short-vector HDC for memory-efficient GNNs

t: NoiseZO: RRAM Noise-Driven Zeroth-Order Optimization for Efficient Forward-Only Training
pb: RRAM compute-in-memory (CIM) training requires gradient computation overhead; RRAM write noise complicates training convergence.
me: NoiseZO maps neural networks to dual RRAM arrays and exploits intrinsic RRAM write noise as zeroth-order perturbations for gradient-free training; fine-grained perturbation control enhances accuracy; training requires only two forward passes per update.
nv: First framework turning RRAM write noise into a feature for zeroth-order gradient estimation during training.
th: RRAM noise-driven forward-only training

t: The Unwritten Contract of Cloud-based Elastic Solid-State Drives
pb: Despite widespread cloud adoption, the performance characteristics and suitability of Elastic SSDs (ESSDs) as local SSD replacements remain uncharacterized, leaving cloud storage users uncertain about deployment decisions.
me: Characterizes two production ESSDs from AWS and Alibaba Cloud through comprehensive benchmarking, identifies counter-intuitive performance patterns, and derives design implications for cloud software optimization to exploit ESSD-specific characteristics.
nv: First comprehensive characterization of ESSD performance contracts revealing counter-intuitive behavior patterns that diverge from local SSD expectations.

mx.other: empirical performance characterization

th: Cloud ESSD performance characterization and design implications

t: NVR: Vector Runahead on NPUs for Sparse Memory Access
pb: Sparse DNNs suffer from irregular memory access patterns causing high cache miss rates and stalls, negating computational benefits of sparsity when dealing with reduced wall-clock execution time.
me: NVR adapts runahead execution to NPU architecture as a decoupled, speculative, lightweight hardware sub-thread that runs ahead to prefetch data, reducing cache misses without requiring compiler support or algorithmic changes; operates with <5% hardware overhead.
nv: Runahead prefetching mechanism specialized for NPU architecture, providing general micro-architectural solution for sparse DNN cache misses without compiler/algorithmic modification.

mx.speedup: 4x average on sparse workloads

th: Runahead prefetching for sparse DNN cache-miss mitigation on NPUs

t: SSDTrain: An Activation Offloading Framework to SSDs for Faster Large Language Model Training
pb: GPU memory capacity growth lags LLM size growth; activations (intermediate tensors from forward pass) dominate GPU memory use during training, limiting micro-batch size and increasing training overhead through expensive weight updates.
me: SSDTrain adaptively offloads activations to high-capacity NVMe SSDs while fully overlapping data transfers with computation, employing tensor deduplication and forwarding optimizations, and integrating with PyTorch, Megatron, and DeepSpeed frameworks.
nv: Adaptive activation offloading to NVMe SSDs with perfect I/O-computation overlap, enabling larger micro-batches and reduced training overhead without sacrificing throughput.
th: Activation offloading to SSD for efficient LLM training

t: PIMoE: Towards Efficient MoE Transformer Deployment on NPU-PIM System through Throttle-Aware Task Offloading
pb: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) Transformer inference suffers from data transfer overhead and imbalanced workload distribution between NPU and processing-in-memory (PIM) components.
me: PIMoE combines NPU and PIM in a heterogeneous system with throttle-aware task offloading to balance workload based on processing capability, and designs a near-memory-controller data condenser to handle sparse data layout translation between NPU and PIM domains.
nv: Throttle-aware dynamic task offloading that adapts workload distribution based on real-time throttling feedback from heterogeneous compute units.

mx.speedup: 4.5x vs A100
mx.other: 1.4x speedup vs SOTA MoE platform

th: heterogeneous MoE inference via adaptive task offloading

t: SSDL-ILT: Efficient ILT utilizing a self-supervised deep learning model
pb: Inverse lithography technology (ILT) for mask optimization is hindered by time-intensive physical simulation; pixel-level mask optimization requires expensive iterative refinement.
me: Proposes self-supervised deep learning model for ILT with novel loss function guiding training without labeled data; model outputs final mask patterns directly, auto-generates sub-resolution assist features (SRAFs) with adjustable complexity.
nv: Self-supervised ILT model eliminating labeled data requirements; automatic SRAF generation with adjustable manufacturability control.

mx.speedup: up to 12,000x vs SOTA models
mx.other: good pattern fidelity and generalization

th: self-supervised learning for inverse lithography technology

t: Efficient Recycling Subspace Truncation Method for Periodic Small-Signal Analysis
pb: Krylov subspace recycling for periodic small-signal RF analysis accelerates simulation but increasing memory cost becomes a bottleneck in large-scale designs; restarting loses recycling benefits.
me: Proposes recycling subspace truncation framework with efficient initial guess selection method and Floquet-based subspace truncation strategy to reduce memory while maintaining iteration benefits.
nv: Floquet-based subspace truncation strategy balancing memory efficiency with recycling benefits in Krylov subspace methods.

mx.speedup: up to 2.5x in same memory cost

th: Floquet-based subspace truncation for efficient RF simulation

t: UniCAIM: A Unified CAM/CIM Architecture with Static-Dynamic KV Cache Pruning for Efficient Long-Context LLM Inference
pb: Transformer LLM inference on long sequences suffers from massive KV cache memory and computation overhead; existing CIM accelerators support only static pruning with fixed patterns or inefficient dynamic pruning.
me: Proposes FeFET-based unified CAM/CIM architecture (UniCAIM) with three computation modes: 1) CAM mode for O(1) dynamic KV pruning via approximate similarity, 2) charge-domain CIM for static pruning with flexible patterns, 3) current-domain for exact attention on pruned KV. Leverages FeFET multi-level storage for signed multibit KV and in-place computation.
nv: First unified CAM/CIM architecture supporting simultaneous static and dynamic KV cache pruning with FeFET multi-level storage for efficient in-place computation.

mx.other: 8.2x to 831x AEDP reduction vs SOTA CIM, comparable accuracy to dense attention

th: unified CAM/CIM for flexible KV cache pruning in LLM inference

t: YOCO: A Hybrid In-Memory Computing Architecture with 8-bit Sub-PetaOps/W In-Situ Multiply Arithmetic for Large-Scale AI
pb: Analog in-memory computing (AiMC) requires efficient 8-bit multiply operations for AI accelerators with high energy efficiency and throughput.
